episodes.170800: Abundant Thunderstorms with storm motions opposite of cell synoptic flow allowed for slow-moving, training storms. This led to areas of flooding and debris flows.
episodes.171239: High pressure remained centered over the Southern Plains which allowed for monsoon moisture to continue to stream into western Colorado. This increase in moisture resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. A localized debris flow occurred in San Miguel County.
episodes.171424: Thunderstorms developed north of a warm front across north-central and northeast Wisconsin during the morning hours on Saturday (8/13).  The strongest storm produced quarter size hail.
episodes.171638: Flash flooding occurred across parts of Albany County Wyoming, including the city of Laramie and the eastern part of the Mullen Burn Scar in southwest Albany County the afternoon of 13 August. Slow moving monsoonal thunderstorms impacted southern Albany County. Fox Creek Road in the eastern Mullen Burn Scar was completely washed out for a 5 mile stretch between Albany and Woods Landing. Additionally, widespread flash flooding was reported in Laramie from separate storms.
episodes.171919: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms moving offshore of the Brevard County coast produced several strong wind gusts.
episodes.171944: A deep moisture surge across Southern California lead to widespread heavy thunderstorms across the mountains and deserts in the middle of August, leading to multiple days of flooding. Torrential downpours lead to severe flash flooding and debris flows near the Apple and El Dorado burn scars.
episodes.172223: SW steering flow ahead of a cold front settling south across GA brought a stronger west coast sea breeze across the local area with the sea breeze merger focused across the eastern tier of SE GA and NE FL in the early evening.
episodes.172224: SW steering flow ahead of a cold front settling south across GA brought a stronger west coast sea breeze across the local area with the sea breeze merger focused across the eastern tier of SE GA and NE FL in the early evening.
episodes.172279: An isolated thunderstorm produced a severe wind gust just west of Ingomar.
episodes.172340: A line of severe thunderstorms moved east across several counties in the Billings Forecast Area. The main impact from these thunderstorms was strong outflow wind gusts.
episodes.173101: A shortwave passing across the region, combined with monsoonal flow and inverted V soundings, resulted in many severe wind gusts in the late afternoon/evening. A single severe hail report was received near Shelby.
episodes.173103: An upper ridge across the region was flanked to the west by a sharp negatively tilted upper trough. Upper jet dynamics were favorable the afternoon of the 13th (Right entrance region) for numerous showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.173291: From August 11-14, thunderstorms produced gusty winds and localized flooding.
episodes.173341: In a classical monsoonal regime, with deep-layered east to southeast flow, high instability (MLCAPE in excess of 1000-1500 J/KG) along with abundant moisture (PWAT 1.8+ inches) resulted in an environment favorable for thunderstorms. An upper-level disturbance moving across Arizona, aided in increasing the areal coverage as well as enhancing the thunderstorm activity.
episodes.173547: The active monsoon pattern continued over northern Arizona. A Flash Flood Watch was in effect from 11 AM MST to 11 PM MST in accordance with the Weather Prediction Center Excessive Rainfall Outlook (slight risk for northern Arizona).
episodes.173591: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona lead to the development of thunderstorms with heavy rain and flash flooding. A flash flood watch was issued for parts of northern Arizona during the late morning through late evening.
episodes.173625: Thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Isolated wind damage occurred in Tucson and Mescal with flash flooding in Oracle and along the Canada Del Oro Wash.
episodes.173631: Two rounds of thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast California, one round during the very early morning hours, between midnight through 4 am local time and another round during the mid to late afternoon hours. The early morning round was instigated by outflow boundaries that moved westward into southeast California from the decaying storm complex across southwest Arizona during the evening hours on the 12th. The environment was characterized by high moisture content (PWATs in excess of 2 inches) and moderate instability (MLCAPE of around 1000 J/KG). The mid to late afternoon round, was a more typical diurnal instigator and the environment once again was conducive, with very high moisture content (PWATs of 2+inches) and high instability (MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/KG).
episodes.173706: A low pressure system off the WA coast continued to push weak waves of instability across Eastern WA. The instability was able to produce mid morning thunderstorms with large hail.
episodes.173730: Typical summer afternoon thunderstorms over the peninsula led to isolated strong wind gusts.
episodes.173797: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Many storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173798: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding.

Video showed Indian Bend Wash running multiple feet deep, resulting in a car nearly submerged by the running flood waters along McCormick Parkway in Scottsdale. The person inside the vehicle had to be rescued by the Fire Department. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along the Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard, located about 3 miles upstream of the incident showed peak flow of 2.92 feet (1875 cfs), which was above alarm stage, at 1640 MST. Additional flow of just over 1000 cfs was likely added to the wash from the Berneil Wash, located about 1 mile upstream of the incident. The gauge along the Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard did not go below alarm stage until just after 2015 MST. No injuries were reported.
The Flagler Inn hotel sign was blown over by thunderstorm winds. The cost of damage was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.
Trees and power lines were blown down by thunderstorm winds. The cost of damage was estimated for inclusion in Storm Data.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along Jackrabbit Wash just downstream of North Vulture Mine Road indicated water levels rising above the alarm stage of 2.9 feet at 1800 MST. The flow peaked at 5.70 feet (6000 cfs) at around 1910 MST.  Impacted area included Wickenburg Road, located about 5 miles downstream of the gauge. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media report (image) received showing a 6 to 8 inch limb that was knocked down west of Vaughn. Size of limb is estimated.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge near the incident showed water levels above alarm stage at 1815 MST, peaking at 4 feet (3397 cfs) at 1924 MST, and dropping below alarm stage at around 2145 MST. No injuries were reported.

Video images from social media showed raging flood waters occurring near Salome Highway just east of US-60. Timing estimated from radar. In addition, the Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge located along Centennial Wash in Wenden showed water levels rising above alarm stage at around 1950 MST, peaking at 3.37 feet (1323 cfs) at around 2034 MST and not going below alarm stage until around 2330 MST. The impacted areas from Centennial Wash include Salome Road, which is located about 4.8 miles downstream of the gauge location in Wenden. No damages or injuries were reported.

Broadcast video showed a lady stuck at a skate park located along the Indian Bend Wash near McDowell Road in Scottsdale. Rescuers unable to get to her for a couple of hours at least due to the flood waters of several feet along the wash. An aerial rescue was performed around 2215 MST. Just 2 miles upstream along the wash near Indian School Road, a Flood County District of Maricopa County gauge reported water levels going above alarm stage after 1830 MST, rising to a record stage of 5.76 feet (3929 cfs) at around 1907 MST. The water level did not go below flood stage until several hours after, at 230 MST on the 13th. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported on Sate Route 98 near K'ai'bii'to.

On the evening of August 12th, Lamoille Canyon received some brief periods of heavy rainfall. The BURN2 site located at the Thomas Canyon Campground in Lamoille Canyon recorded 0.34 inches that fell over a 15-minute span from 2100 to 2115LT. The area continued to get some more rain and ended up with 0.49 inches in 1 hour from 2100 to 2200 LT. Shortly thereafter a debris flow was reported in the area by a hydrologist from the USGS. Some water, mud, silt, and small rocks washed over the road depositing the silt and mud on the roadway. The hydrologist reiterated that 0.25 inches for 15 minutes or 1 inch/hr seem to be a good threshold for debris flows to occur.
A motor home was stuck in major flooding on Amboy Road near Schooler Road, and multiple vehicles were stuck on Amboy Road near Godwin Road.
Highway 95 was flooded near mile marker 71.

Several mudslides occurred on Black Bear Pass and the nearby Bridal Veil Road and Bridal Veil Trail as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms. An abundance of boulders and mud accumulated on the pass. Water flowed down from the peak and across the road below. Eight vehicles and fifteen occupants were stranded as a result of the debris flows. The pass and roads remained closed for several days for cleanup operations.
Widespread standing water on State Highway 79 and San Felipe Road. Radar estimated 1.0 to 2.8 inches of rain within three hours.

Widespread flash flooding across the city with heavy rainfall from stationary thunderstorms. Numerous CoCoRaHS observers across the city measured between 1.5 to 2.75 inches of rainfall. Flooding was ongoing from 22nd Street to 1st Street and from Harney Street south to Spring Creek.
Several roads in Golden Valley were closed.
Heavy rain caved in the roof of the Safeway store.

Numerous trees were blown down on Andy Devine Ave near I-40.

One to 3 inches of heavy rain fell in much of Fremont County causing extensive flooding.  15 people were stranded east/southeast of Macks Inn along the Henry's fork River between Big Springs and Macks Inn due to the rain.   Many were suffering hypothermia and were treated on scene.  Multiple private roads on the Ashton Hill were washing out.  A running track was flooded at North Fremont High School.   Moving water was filmed across fields and roads in the area of N 3700 E and E 1400 N.  Crops and fields suffered damage in the Marysville area.  Several sections of the Ashton-Tetonia Rail Trail were flooded, washed out and covered in mud.  3 cabins reported flooded north northwest of Squirrel.  The Henrys Fork River rose one half foot between 5:45 Pm MDT and 9 PM MDT.
Some shingles were blown off a building and one inch tree limbs were broken.
Highway 78 near Milepost 53 was flooded, with multiple vehicles stuck in the floodwaters. No damages or injuries were reported.
